# K10.1 Fused QK RMSNorm + RoPE (NVIDIA `opt_kernels`), with Q, K, V packed and the amax

Classification: Internal (becomes public with the MLPerf Training v6.1 results)

[Index](../KERNELS.md) · Switches: `OPT_QKNORM_ROPE=1`, `OPT_QKNORM_ROPE_STRICT=1`
(`config_GB300_2x4x3xtp1pp1cp1ep1_nvfp4_v7.sh` L134-135) · Class: **Bitwise** against NVIDIA's reference kernel
(Q, K, V, dX, dγ); NVIDIA's kernel itself is **Same function** as Megatron's separate RMSNorm + RoPE · Rule basis: TR-8.3

## 1. Packages

| | G6c |
|---|---|
| Switches | `OPT_QKNORM_ROPE=1` (L134), `OPT_QKNORM_ROPE_STRICT=1` (L135); `FUSED_QKV_ROPE="True"` (L39); `OPT_QKNORM_ROPE_SELFCHECK` and the tile variables `OPT_QKNORM_ROPE_*_ROWS`, `_CTAS`, `_WARPS` not set (defaults 1; 32, 32, 8, 4, 4) |
| Uses | `NVFP4_QKV_PACKED=1`, `NVFP4_QKV_PACKED_AMAX=1` (L132-133, K8.6) |
| Model | `qk_layernorm` True, `rmsnorm_eps` 1e-6 (`conf/gpt_oss.yaml` L37, L39); 64 query heads, 8 KV groups, head dim 64 (`pretrain.py` L1072–1075) |
| Code | `opt_kernels/qknorm_rope.py`, `opt_kernels/qknorm_rope_patch.py` (NVIDIA); `firmus_kernels/qknorm_rope_packed.py`; `pretrain.py` L62–69, L1137–1139 |

`opt_kernels/` is byte-identical to `nemo_g1_1012/opt_kernels/`, NVIDIA's 20261012 reference implementation as
submitted unchanged (`nemo_g1_1012/README.md`), which imports it the same way (`nemo_g1_1012/pretrain.py` L48,
L219–221) and sets `FUSED_QKV_ROPE=True` (`nemo_g1_1012/config_common.sh` L47). That recipe leaves `OPT_QKNORM_ROPE_STRICT`
unset (default 0). G6c is the only package with this item.

## 2. What the reference does

The reference model has an RMSNorm on q and on k of each attention layer (`qk_layernorm`). Megatron's composed path
splits the fused QKV projection output, runs TE `RMSNorm` on q and on k (BF16 out), then TE's fused RoPE on q and k
(`apply_rope_fusion`, BF16 out); v passes through. NVIDIA's reference implementation replaces this with its Triton
kernel when `opt_kernels.qknorm_rope_patch` is active (`ACTIVE`, L261): `pretrain.py` then sets
`fused_single_qkv_rope=True` and `apply_rope_fusion=False` (G6c L1137–1139, the same expressions as NVIDIA's
L219–221), the q/k norm modules are retyped to a pass-through class (`_init`, L54–68), and Megatron's
`apply_fused_qkv_rotary_pos_emb` is replaced by `_dispatch` (L167–216), which calls `qknorm_rope` with the norm
weights. The upstream Megatron and TE sources are not in the package.

## 3. What this implementation does

1. NVIDIA's code runs unchanged: `pretrain.py` L62 imports the patch, which installs itself at import because
   `OPT_QKNORM_ROPE=1` (L19, L265–266).
2. `pretrain.py` L64–69: with the patch active and `NVFP4_QKV_PACKED=1`, `firmus_kernels/qknorm_rope_packed.py`
   `install` (L157–166) installs TE's `nvfp4_qkv_packed` (K8.6) and replaces `opt_kernels.qknorm_rope.qknorm_rope`,
   the function `_dispatch` and the self-check call, with its own `qknorm_rope` (L150–151).
3. Forward (`QKNormRoPEPacked.forward`, L136–145; `packed_fwd`, L108–131): one `new_empty` buffer holds Q, K and V
   back to back (L113–116). `_qknorm_rope_fwd_amax_kernel` (L29–105) is NVIDIA's `_qknorm_rope_fwd_kernel`
   (`qknorm_rope.py` L50–120) with the same grid, rows per program and warps (`_nv._FWD_ROWS`, `_FWD_WARPS`), plus
   one store per program of the max |output| (L102–105): |BF16 Q or K output|, |x| for V (V is the input). The
   buffer's storage pointer and the parts go to K8.6's `_last` (L139–140), where the FP8 attention input quantize
   takes them (K8.6 steps 3–4).
4. Backward: NVIDIA's `QKNormRoPE.backward` (L147; `qknorm_rope.py` L430–442), on the same saved tensors.
5. `OPT_QKNORM_ROPE_STRICT=1` turns every fallback of NVIDIA's patch into an error: non-retypable norm modules
   (L66–67), an untagged QKV tensor (L180–182), an unsupported shape or a failed self-check (L161–163, L212–213).

## 4. Why the result is the same

The Firmus forward is NVIDIA's kernel body with the output pointers moved into one buffer and an extra reduction
that reads values the kernel already computed; the arithmetic of Q, K, V is unchanged, and the backward is
NVIDIA's. Measured: Q, K, V, dX, dγ bit-identical to NVIDIA's kernel (section 8). Class **Bitwise** against NVIDIA's
kernel. The parts are maxima of the stored BF16 values, so their max equals `max |q|k|v|` exactly, except with NaN:
`tl.maximum` drops NaN where `torch.max` returns NaN (section 8).

NVIDIA's kernel against Megatron's composed path is Same function (E1): RMSNorm in FP32, gain, RoPE with FP32
cos/sin tables (`_qknorm_sincos_kernel`, L33–47), one BF16 rounding (L107–108) instead of one after the norm and one
after RoPE. The reference implementation accepts that difference by its own self-check: max relative error ≤ 2⁻⁶,
mean relative error ≤ 2⁻⁹, V equal (`qknorm_rope_patch.py` L135–141).

## 5. Numerics

BF16 x and gains, FP32 arithmetic, `rsqrt(mean(x²) + eps)` per 64-wide head row (L88–89), BF16 outputs. dγ: FP32
per-program partials reduced in two passes (`qknorm_colsum`, L396–406), deterministic. The amax parts are FP32.
Triton compiles at run time; no compiler options are set.

## 6. Shapes and fallbacks

- **Gate:** NVIDIA's `_retypable` (L43–51: TE `RMSNorm` with 64 weights) and `_unsupported` (L87–101): 4-D BF16
  contiguous QKV, split `[nq·64, 64, 64]`, KV groups and query heads per group powers of two, sbhd, no start
  positions, not interleaved, CP 1, FP32 contiguous freqs; `_check_inputs` asserts the same and `numel < 2³¹`
  (`qknorm_rope.py` L284–292). The training call: 8 groups × 8 query heads (`[8192, 3, 8, 640]`).
- **Falls back:** upstream, to the composed path (L214–216), logged once; here every fallback raises (step 5).
  The packed install is skipped silently if the patch is not active (`pretrain.py` L64).
- **Assumes:** that the self-check of the first eligible call, run outside graph capture (L199–206), represents
  later calls; with `OPT_QKNORM_ROPE_SELFCHECK=1` it checks the forward only (the backward needs ≥ 2, L146).
- **Check:** config L134-135. In all 10 `results/firmus_gb300_ngpu8_gptoss_g6c_nvfp4_v2_2/gpt_oss_20b/result_*.txt`:
  `[opt qknorm_rope] installed` (`result_0.txt` L216), `FIRMUS qknorm_rope packed installed (amax 1)` (L218),
  `[opt qknorm_rope] selfcheck fwd q rel 5.85e-03/1.47e-03 k rel 6.62e-03/1.47e-03 v equal True ok` (L1038, values
  of `result_0.txt`), `[opt qknorm_rope] first forward: retyped=48 fused=24 fallback=0` (L1065), and K8.6's
  `NVFP4_QKV_PACKED stats {'packed': 64, 'fallback': 0, 'amax': 64}` (L2276), which shows the parts of this kernel
  were used for every FP8 quantize of Q, K, V.

## 8. Tests and evidence

Kernel test on this package's image (Firmus test script `k10_1_qknorm_rope_packed.py`, available on request): the
Firmus `qknorm_rope` and `packed_fwd` against NVIDIA's `qknorm_rope`, outputs q, k, v, dx, dgq, dgk, and the max of
the parts against `max |q|k|v|` of NVIDIA's outputs; errors vs FP64 are recorded per case.

- Job 22900, runs a and b rc 0, 126 cases per run, 2 with a difference: `fixture_zero_centered_vs_not` (by design,
  3 of 6 outputs, 226 469 297 elements) and `specials:amax` (1 element: NaN inputs, the reference amax is NaN, the
  parts' max is not). Every other case 0 differ: seeded and random training shape, zero-centred gains, `linear_qkv`
  outputs captured in this package's training run (job 22873), finite and non-finite specials (the non-finite
  outputs are equal), constant rows, zero input, inputs × 10⁴, shapes 1×1, 7×2, 8191, 8193, 4 groups, 1 query head
  per group, 1 group × 16 heads, packed layout with and without the amax, prefill 0x00 / 0xFF, fresh process, NVIDIA
  vs NVIDIA control. Run a vs run b: 413 digests equal, 0 differ.
- With NaN in Q, K or V the scale differs from a `torch.max` reference; the same `tl.maximum` reduction in K8.6's
  test gave FP8 data and `scale_inv` equal to TE's own amax pass with one NaN input (job 22882, K8.6).
- compute-sanitizer on this image (`../KERNELS.md` section 9.1): memcheck, full test, job 22863: 14 errors, 7
  `CUDA API Error` (`cudaVersion` 13041 exceeds driver 13040) and 7 `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE` on
  `cuGetProcAddress_v2`, no memory access errors; initcheck (job 22866) 0 errors and racecheck (job 22867) 0 hazards
  on the small case (`KT_SMALL=1`).
- Run log: the lines of Check, in all 10 scored runs.

## 9. Open points

1. The errors vs FP64 of NVIDIA's and the Firmus kernel are in the test records (available on request) and are not
   quoted here; the bitwise equality to NVIDIA's kernel makes them equal by construction.
2. The FP8 quantize that consumes the parts (K8.6 steps 3–4) is tested on this image with K5.2's packed forward
   (job 22882), not with this kernel; the chain is shown by the stats line of Check, not by a test.
3. Earlier runs of this test (jobs 22854, 22857) ended with rc 1 after 2 cases; the reruns 22862 and 22900 completed.
   The cause is not recorded in the test output.
